entries.note: Two of the six extended tools cannot be gated where the others are. The runtime supervisor answers /api/update-workspace and /api/desktop-action itself and forwards everything else to the workspace worker, so update_workspace and reload_desktop never reach the worker's gate and read the ledger here instead, before the call. The capability half is separate and applies to all six: agentToken says the worker serves a ledger, so an identified agent against a worker that does not advertise it is refused naming the layer to update rather than calling a worker that would pass every request. An anonymous caller — probeTools, an older launch with no identity — is not an agent and is never gated at all, which is what keeps update_workspace able to prepare its own replacement.

Script execution is effectful and not idempotent; root-bound tools require an explicit script path, literal argv and a target desktop. View attachment failure returns a retained process identity. show_session attaches that process without another execution, and ordinary stop_session remains the explicit termination action.

entries.note: preview_file runs the project's own declared executable, so it is open-world and not read-only even though it never writes. The route returns the whole sanitized tree; the tool slices dir/depth and pages files with offset/limit, then shrinks depth and limit until the serialized reply fits the 32,000-character budget, reporting truncated/nextOffset (review finding 5). Command metadata is made root-relative and the generic tool wrapper replaces the absolute root path in error text with <root>. Entry text is bounded like read_file; the hex window is dropped because agents get size and SHA-256 instead.

dashboard_actions is read-only (availability only); dashboard_capture is open-world because it runs a project executable and writes files. Script and log actions deliberately get no new tool: scripts go through open_script with the listed script/args/env, logs start from the desktop tab and are followed with show_session/session_output, so process creation stays on the existing audited paths.

game_preflight and launch_game address only the games the bound project declares in .rengine/project.json; their descriptions name no game, and the connector never carries a built-in executable or data path. Both take an optional gameId and default to the first declared record, so a single-game project needs no argument while a multi-game one is addressed explicitly and an unknown id is answered with the declared ids. launch_game is open-world because it executes the project's own program; it returns the running session of that same game id when one exists, so agents inspect the returned id rather than assuming a fresh process, and two declared games of one project can be running at once. The removed nolf_preflight/launch_nolf have no alias: nothing had shipped them to a user. The two tools gate on two capabilities, because the workspace layer can deliver only one of them: game_preflight needs projectGame, which the replaceable worker advertises for the route it serves itself, while launch_game needs projectGameLaunch, which only a session host that answers from the declaration can offer — replacing that host requires quiescence, so the refusal names it instead of telling the agent to update the workspace layer again.

The devices tool is readOnlyHint (it changes nothing in the project) but openWorldHint, because it reaches the network or a USB device. Its description deliberately does NOT claim read-only: adb get-state and adb devices start the adb server when no daemon is running, so a probe is bounded and side-effect-light, not free of side effects. It also states that reachable is not launchable — a green ssh probe still cannot create a GL context in a logon session with no window station — so an agent does not read a reachable device as permission to launch on it. It gates on projectDevices, which the replaceable workspace worker advertises (KI-043: a capability served only by the retained host cannot be delivered by a layered update). The description now also states what each bound target carries — an action's availability as the dashboard computed it, a game's preflight — because the Devices tab renders those as controls and an agent reading this tool should not need a second listing to learn what can be run where.

New window and report tools retain the connector’s captured root. Opening a window attaches an existing root-bound agent; only the recorded origin/project pair can inspect its window or exchange reports. The origin can explicitly view its linked project inbox or attribute its own project-side observation without claiming another agent wrote it.
